summary: The code has a critical syntax error, an empty main() that does not execute the simulation, and incomplete metric compilation. It diverges from the specified task in entities, parameters, and required metrics. Some logic and performance issues are also present.

issues.description: Incomplete statement 'adoption_by' at the end of _finalize_metrics causes a SyntaxError and prevents the file from importing or running.
issues.solution: Complete the computation of adoption_by_quintile and the Gini inequality metric, then return a metrics dict. Remove the stray 'adoption_by' token.

issues.description: main() is empty and does not run the simulation or output results.
issues.location: Function main() at top of file
issues.solution: Implement main() to parse optional arguments or load parameters, instantiate MaskAdoptionSimulation, call run(), and print JSON results.

issues.description: Finalization of metrics is incomplete; no return statement is present due to the syntax error. Required metrics are not produced.
issues.solution: Finish building the metrics dictionary per specification (overall_adoption_rate, subgroup_adoption_rate, time_to_threshold, sustained_adoption, policy_compliance_rate, infections_averted if disease enabled, R_effective, enforcement_actions, mask_access_inequality) and return it.

issues.description: Mismatch with specification: entities, attributes, and behaviors diverge (e.g., Organization vs Government, MaskMarket vs Retailer, GlobalContext missing). Several required parameters are not supported (e.g., supply_shock_probability, subsidy_budget_per_day, disease_module_enabled).
issues.location: Classes and parameters across the file
issues.solution: Align class names/attributes with the spec or provide adapter logic mapping the spec parameters to current ones. Implement GlobalContext and MaskMarket or equivalent behavior including supply shocks, subsidies, and disease module toggling.

issues.description: Required metrics are missing or only partially implemented: subgroup_adoption_rate, sustained_adoption, policy_compliance_rate, infections_averted, enforcement_actions (time series), mask_access_inequality.
issues.solution: Track and compute required metrics. For example: policy_compliance_rate as share of agents wearing masks when mask_required is true; enforcement_actions as time series of warnings/fines; mask_access_inequality via Gini of mask_supply or adoption by SES.

issues.description: Household lookup is O(N^2) during setup due to repeated linear search in _find_household_id when assigning incomes/quintiles.
issues.location: Method _setup_entities calls _find_household_id inside list comprehension for incomes
issues.solution: Precompute and store a direct person_id -> household_id mapping (e.g., a list of size N) during household creation and use it instead of searching.

issues.description: Stockout day counting is incorrect. It checks inventory before and after restock only and ignores depletion to zero during the day.
issues.solution: Track inventory at end of day; increment stockout_days if retailer.inventory == 0 after purchases. Alternatively track if inventory hits zero at any point during the day.

issues.description: Mask consumption decrements on day 0 due to modulo logic, which may prematurely consume initial stock.
issues.solution: Start replacement after the first interval (e.g., if (self.day + 1) % interval == 0) or track last_replacement_day per person.

issues.description: Disease module always runs; there is no toggle like disease_module_enabled as per spec.
issues.solution: Add a parameter toggle and wrap transmission and related metrics accordingly. If disabled, skip infection updates and related metrics.

issues.description: Multiple functions include extraneous 'pass' statements before functional code, which is harmless but confusing.
issues.location: Various functions (sigmoid, gini_coefficient, default_parameters, validate_parameters, build_network, __init__, _setup_entities, etc.)
issues.solution: Remove unnecessary 'pass' statements in functions that already contain code.

issues.description: Unused imports (argparse, sys, json currently unused because main() is empty).
issues.solution: Either implement main() to use these imports or remove unused imports to reduce clutter.

issues.description: Limited validation of input parameters and no try/except around network generation or JSON output.
issues.solution: Expand parameter validation (e.g., ensure non-negative prices, valid masks), guard network building with informative errors, and handle JSON serialization errors in main().
